questions.background: The Mubadala DC Open is a professional tennis tournament in Washington, D.C. Its men's singles competition is part of the ATP Tour.

No. 3 Taylor Fritz jumps sharply (0.135 -> 0.20) after cruising past Zizou Bergs 6-3, 6-4 unbroken: he already needs only 4 wins and his entire Quarter 2 cleared out (R2 vs Majchrzak instead of Paul; QF vs Michelsen or Mannarino instead of Tien/Draper). No. 2 Ben Shelton rises (0.130 -> 0.165) with both Tiafoe and Fils eliminated from his bottom half, though he still must play R1 vs qualifier Martin Damm Tuesday evening and faces R1 winner Ugo Humbert in R2. No. 1 Alex de Minaur trims slightly (0.095 -> 0.090): he still faces nemesis Stefanos Tsitsipas (Gstaad champ, lopsided H2H) Tuesday night, though the winner gets an easy R2 against world No. 612 teen Cruz Hewitt. No. 4 Lorenzo Musetti enters at 0.070 (replacing eliminated Tiafoe) after advancing past Matteo Arnaldi (6-0, 3-1 ret.) into a Fils-free Quarter 3, while No. 7 Jakub Mensik inches up (0.055 -> 0.060) ahead of his R1 vs Trevor Svajda. Remaining 41.5% covers Ugo Humbert, Stefanos Tsitsipas, Rafael Jodar, Brandon Nakashima, Alex Michelsen, Terence Atmane, and the rest of the draw.

questions.title: Which country will agree to a joint project with Iran to clear sea mines from the Strait of Hormuz by August 26, 2026?
questions.background: Sea mines have been reported near the Strait of Hormuz, a major route for international oil and gas shipments.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the country that agrees with Iran to a joint mine-clearance project in the Strait of Hormuz, as announced in a statement from the two governments by August 26, 2026. Resolution Date : 2026-08-26 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: Important July 28 diplomatic updates (Reuters/Straits Times, Al Jazeera, Khaleej Times, Irish Times): amid a third straight night of halted US-Iran airstrikes, Iran and Oman formally exchanged written proposals on reopening and managing the Strait of Hormuz — Oman proposed a Malacca-style joint regional mechanism with voluntary fees, while Iran's Deputy FM Kazem Gharibabadi counter-proposed a temporary Iran-Oman transit arrangement. Crucially, Gharibabadi explicitly warned that Tehran 'would not allow any third country, even if invited by Oman, to de-mine the Strait of Hormuz' (as the US and UK discuss a Western demining coalition in London), while Al Jazeera reports Tehran is privately showing 'some flexibility' in step-by-step bilateral talks with Muscat even though mine-clearance responsibility remains a point of contention. Because Oman is the sole co-littoral state negotiating directly with Tehran and Iran just publicly ruled out third-country demining participation, Oman strengthens meaningfully (0.37 -> 0.44, still moderated below 0.50 since no joint mine-clearance pact is signed and Tehran currently prefers unilateral clearance). Third-country alternatives trim modestly: China (0.25 -> 0.22), Pakistan (0.16 -> 0.14), and Russia (0.09 -> 0.08), with Japan held at 0.02 and 10% residual for UAE, Turkey, India, Qatar, or others.

questions.title: Which club will Mohamed Salah join first after leaving Liverpool at the end of the 2025–26 season?
questions.background: Mohamed Salah has announced that he will leave Liverpool at the end of the season.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official announcement from Salah or his new club, or reliable news reporting confirming a completed signing. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the first club with which Salah signs a senior playing contract following his departure from Liverpool at the end of the 2025–26 season. Transfer speculation, negotiations, and trial appearances do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the club.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-28 deepening of the Besiktas impasse and rival-suitor clarification: full transcripts of Besiktas sporting director Onder Ozen's press conference (Football365, Liverpool.com, Transfermarkt) confirm Besiktas have 'shelved' the Salah file, President Serdal Adali 'stepped away from the table for now,' and the club will make no further offer ('take-it-or-leave-it'), explicitly criticizing agent Ramy Abbas for demanding an allegedly illegal commission rate (Sabah July 28 reports EUR 5M commission plus 50% of Turkish shirt sales and 100% of international/Egypt shirt profits) while noting Salah's camp said 'they're in talks with another club as well.' Fabrizio Romano (July 28 YouTube) corroborated that 'nothing is agreed yet' with a 'big difference' on salary/contract, while Salah assesses proposals from MLS and Saudi Arabia. Cutting Besiktas 0.38 -> 0.28 (retaining plurality since their final offer stays on the table, Ozen pointedly appealed past Abbas to Salah himself, and Romano did not close the door). Replacing Juventus (0.05, zero July links; TEAMtalk reports European stay unlikely) with Sporting Kansas City at 0.14 after The Athletic identified Egyptian-American-owned SKC as MLS pole-position frontrunners and SI.com (July 28) confirmed SKC has a 'lucrative' two-year offer actively awaiting a response. Among Saudi Pro League clubs (window opened July 23), nudging Jeddah-based Al-Ahli 0.13 -> 0.14 (Sky Sports link as Riyad Mahrez successor, 2-hour flight to Cairo), trimming Al-Hilal 0.13 -> 0.12 (ESPN/Michael Edwards link tempered by Al-Hilal's July 26 $73.4M signing of winger Crysencio Summerville per Arab News), and holding Al-Ittihad at 0.10, with 22% residual for San Diego FC (owned by Egyptian billionaire Sir Mohamed Mansour), Al-Qadsiah/Neom SC/Al-Nassr, and other Turkish/European clubs.

questions.title: Who will win Michigan’s 2026 Democratic primary for U.S. Senate?
questions.background: Michigan will elect a U.S. senator in November 2026. The Democratic primary will determine the party’s nominee for that election.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Results from Michigan election authorities or unambiguous reporting by major news organizations identifying the winner of Michigan’s 2026 Democratic primary for U.S. Senate. Resolution Date : Resolve when the winner of the primary, scheduled for August 4, 2026, is publicly established. Accepted Answer Format : The winning candidate’s name.
questions.current_reasoning: Strong market and post-debate update on July 28 (Newsweek, CBS News, MLive, Roll Call): our July 24 drop from 0.63 to 0.51 overreacted to Gov. Gretchen Whitmer's endorsement of Haley Stevens before observing market/voter reaction. Four days after Whitmer's endorsement and immediately following Monday night's final Fox 2 Detroit debate — where El-Sayed effectively hammered Stevens over $46M-$60M in AIPAC/United Democracy Project outside spending (a potent liability in Michigan's 2026 Democratic primary amid the unpopular US-Israel war with Iran) — BOTH liquid prediction markets surged in El-Sayed's favor on Tuesday morning: Kalshi jumped from 64% (July 26) to 71% El-Sayed / 30% Stevens (~70.3% devigged) and Polymarket jumped from 65% to 72% El-Sayed / 30% Stevens (~70.6% devigged). Still, no new post-Whitmer primary horse-race poll has been published, the non-partisan July 8-11 Detroit News/Glengariff poll had Stevens ahead 48-41 (strong with older, Black, and early absentee voters), Stevens holds endorsements from Whitmer, Peters, Stabenow, and Granholm plus massive late TV spending, and she touted a July 22-24 Glengariff general-election poll showing her stronger against Mike Rogers (46-45 vs El-Sayed trailing 39-49). Blending the ~70.5% real-money markets with modest shrinkage for Glengariff, Whitmer's late push, and absentee turnout shifts the forecast from 0.51/0.49 to Abdul El-Sayed 0.65, Haley Stevens 0.35.

questions.title: What sentence will Egyptian television presenter Sarah Khalifa receive at trial in her drug-trafficking case?
questions.background: Sarah Khalifa was arrested in Egypt in April 2025 as part of a drug investigation.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The trial court’s announced judgment in the drug-trafficking prosecution stemming from Khalifa’s April 2025 arrest, as confirmed by official court information or reliable reporting from Al-Ahram. Resolution Timing : Resolve when the trial court announces its verdict and sentence. Later appellate decisions and judgments in unrelated cases do not count. Accepted Answer Format : Provide a short legal term identifying the principal penalty imposed, or the court’s disposition if no penalty is imposed. If multiple penalties are imposed, report the most severe.
questions.current_reasoning: Major procedural and legal update from July 8-9 Arabic court reporting (Al-Ahram, Masrawy, Al-Ain, Newsroom): on July 9, the New Cairo Criminal Court adjourned the trial of Sarah Khalifa and 27 co-defendants directly to August 4, 2026 WITHOUT referring the case papers to the Grand Mufti. Under Article 381(2) of Egypt's Code of Criminal Procedure, a criminal court cannot pronounce a death sentence without first referring the file to the Grand Mufti and adjourning weeks later for final sentencing—meaning a death sentence cannot legally be handed down on August 4. Substantively, two further disclosures weaken capital sentencing: (1) Masrawy's indictment summary confirms Khalifa is Defendant #4 (financier/coordinator, plus personal drug-use and unlicensed firearms charges), behind fugitive ringleaders #1 and #2; and (2) defense counsel invoked a Supreme Constitutional Court ruling invalidating scheduling decrees by the Head of the Egyptian Drug Authority. However, the 3-member forensic committee and forensic expert testified on July 8-9 that 2018-2019 Minister of Health decrees explicitly schedule narcotics 'analogues' and confirmed the lab analysis was technically sound, while the court firmly rejected defense procedural challenges. Accordingly, cutting Death penalty sharply 0.28 -> 0.06 (retaining 6% only if the court issues a Mufti referral on Aug 4 for a later verdict), lifting Life imprisonment 0.46 -> 0.56 as the primary statutory penalty under Narcotics Law Art. 33, raising Aggravated imprisonment 0.13 -> 0.19 (Art. 17 clemency or lesser trafficking/firearms counts), Acquittal 0.07 -> 0.11 (Constitutional Court scheduling defense), and Imprisonment 0.04 -> 0.06 (conviction only on drug use/minor counts), with 2% residual.
